title: Poison Help line
what: Talk to a poison expert about something a child swallowed, breathed in or got on their skin.
who: Anyone in the United States, any time. Call 911 instead if a child can't be woken or isn't breathing.

title: 2-1-1 Texas
what: A free information and referral line for food, health, housing and other local help.
who: Anyone in Texas. Phone and live chat are offered in English and Spanish.
source_publisher: 2-1-1 Texas (Texas Health and Human Services Commission)

title: Texas WIC
what: Help buying healthy food, plus nutrition support, for pregnancy and early childhood.
who: Pregnant or breastfeeding women and families with children younger than 5. Eligibility rules apply.

title: YourTexasBenefits
what: The state's online place to apply for food (SNAP), cash help (TANF), health care and WIC benefits.
who: Texas families who may qualify for state benefits. TANF is for families with children 18 and younger.

title: Children's Medicaid and CHIP
what: Low-cost or free health coverage for children and teens.
who: Texas children whose families meet income and household rules.

title: Car seat check-up events and stations
what: Find a car seat check-up event or inspection station, with local experts who help with installation.
who: Any caregiver who wants a car seat checked or installed correctly.

title: Cribs for Kids
what: Portable cribs and safe sleep education for babies whose families can't afford a safe place to sleep.
who: Families who can't afford a safe sleep space. Use the site's partner finder or call to ask about local help.

title: Free smoke alarms (Austin)
what: Austin firefighters install a smoke alarm for free and do a free home hazards assessment.
who: Austin residents in need who live in a privately owned home. Call and leave your name, address and phone number.

title: Postpartum Support International HelpLine
what: A helpline for families dealing with pregnancy and postpartum challenges. It does not handle emergencies.
who: Parents and families. Call 1-800-944-4773 (Spanish: press 1) or text HELP to 800-944-4773; 8am to 11pm Eastern.

title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
what: Free, confidential emotional support by call, text or chat for anyone in distress, any time.
who: Anyone, including caregivers in crisis. Call or text 988. Spanish is available for text and chat.

title: Head Start
what: Early learning programs for young children. Search for a center by zip code, city or state.
who: Families with young children. Call 1-866-763-6481 to ask about eligibility.
source_publisher: Head Start (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services)

title: Find licensed child care in Texas
what: Look up child care providers in Texas.
who: Texas parents choosing a child care provider.

title: Help paying for child care (Texas Workforce Commission)
what: State child care services that can help working families pay for care.
who: Texas families who need child care. Check the page for eligibility.
